t: A stem duchy of northern Germany between the Rhine and the Elbe, ruled by the Liudolfing, Billung, Welf and Ascanian families.
Its dukes became German kings and emperors, from Henry the Fowler in 919 through the Ottonians to Lothair III.
Henry the Lion made it a near-royal power, but his fall in 1180 broke up the duchy, which was finally divided around 1296.
dyk: The bronze lion that Henry the Lion set up in Brunswick around 1166 is often described as the first large free-standing hollow-cast sculpture made north of the Alps since antiquity.
ev: Count Liudolf and Oda found the convent of Gandersheim
Duke Henry is elected king of East Francia
Henry the Fowler defeats the Magyars at Riade
Saxon princes defeat Emperor Henry V at Welfesholz
Henry the Lion refounds Lübeck on the Baltic
Frederick Barbarossa deposes Henry the Lion and divides Saxony
The duchy splits into Saxe-Lauenburg and Saxe-Wittenberg

f.capital: No fixed capital; Brunswick under Henry the Lion
f.successor: Duchy of Saxe-Lauenburg; Duchy of Saxe-Wittenberg; Duchy of Westphalia
